rationale: All three missed cases share the same pattern: a company that is only weeks old (well under 90 days) yet declares share capital of 75 M or more. Setting max_age_days=90 captures "weeks-old" entities with a comfortable buffer while staying well below the 1825-day ceiling, avoiding misfires on legitimately young but well-capitalised subsidiaries of large groups (which would typically be incorporated with a deliberate, documented capital injection and would clear other checks). Setting max_capital=75,000,000 matches the stated evidence floor exactly — a normal SME incorporated at any age would almost never legitimately open with 75 M+ in declared share capital, so the false-positive risk is low.
